title: The strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture
formal: Does every 3-connected planar graph admit a planar straight-line greedy embedding with convex faces?
context:
Greedy means that for each ordered pair of distinct vertices s,t, some neighbor of s lies closer to t than s does. The weaker existence of a greedy embedding alone has been proved.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Asks whether planar convex geometry can also support delivery by purely local greedy routing.
